headline: California has made it law that driverless-taxi companies can be fined when their cars block emergency crews for more than 30 minutes.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 by 2: the signing was already carried in our 1 Oct 2026 edition, and Mashable adds detail rather than a new event.
importance_line: Emergency crews and residents in California gain a financial penalty for robotaxis that block rescue work, but the article gives no fine amount and enforcement is untested.
summary: Mashable reports that California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed SB 1246, under which operators such as Waymo and Tesla face fines if their driverless vehicles block first responders for more than 30 minutes, and which also requires two-way communication with emergency departments and company-hired local incident technicians who can respond to stalled vehicles. The law was signed by about 30 Sep 2026 and we carried the signing on 1 Oct 2026 from Senator Dave Cortese's office; Mashable adds the fines and the background of earlier complaints about robotaxis obstructing emergency vehicles.
notes: Signing date from a Cortese release dated 30 Sep 2026 (search listing) and Mashable's 'last week'. Repeat of our 1 Oct item; the final duplicate check should treat it as old news.
